add-a-field.current_function: Adds or changes a custom field (text/number/date/dropdown) on a CRM record (opportunity/contact/company) in CRM settings, then optionally surfaces it on the live opportunity-card display and adds it as a column in the relevant workspace spreadsheet — letting the operator self-serve a field change end to end. Respects the 202 approval gate.
add-a-field.standalone_value: None as a standalone skill. The core deliverable is a schema mutation on a live CRM record store: create a custom field, then wire it onto the live pipeline card display and into the live workspace spreadsheet. Every step is a CRM write — there is no offline artifact, pasted-data transform, or reasoning output a no-tools owner could use. A "custom field" has no meaning without a record store to attach values to; "show it on the opportunity card" and "add it to the workspace spreadsheet" are pure live-workspace writes; and the 202 queued-for-approval handling is itself a CRM-platform concept. Strip the CRM and nothing useful remains.
add-a-field.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The skill requires TrustPager's custom-field/CRM-settings tools to create the field, the pipeline card-display config to surface it, and the workspace spreadsheet (via /build-spreadsheet) to add the column. It belongs entirely behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section; with no CRM connected the skill cannot run at all.

assemble-pack.current_function: Combines a record's filled forms and uploaded files into one ordered PDF pack (lender/insurer/council submission), then saves it back to the opportunity. Lists candidates via list_opportunity_files + list_opportunity_documents, confirms contents/order with the operator, then merges with bundle_files. Gathers only — does not send.
assemble-pack.standalone_value: The core value — merging a set of related source documents into one ordered submission PDF — is a platform-agnostic document operation. Standalone, the owner points at a local folder of filled forms and scanned uploads; the skill lists them, confirms order, and merges into one named pack via the BOS PDF tooling. Real minute-one-ish win with nothing connected.
assemble-pack.tp_enhancement: TrustPager auto-discovers candidates on the live opportunity (portal client uploads via list_opportunity_files, auto-archived filled-form PDFs and signed envelopes via list_opportunity_documents), de-dupes across both libraries, and writes the finished pack back onto the deal record for handoff to /send-email or /send-for-signing.

audit-my-automations.current_function: Health-checks every automation in the connected CRM workspace: pulls each automation's structure (triggers, actions, dedup/daily-cap settings) plus its recent run log via read-only TrustPager endpoints, computes per-automation flags (recent_failures, never_run, stale, mostly_skipped, sends_without_dedup, webhook_without_daily_cap, no_actions/no_triggers) and cross-automation trigger overlaps, presents the report worst-first, then offers safe mechanical write-backs (turn on dedup, set a daily cap, disable a duplicate) with per-item approval.
audit-my-automations.standalone_value: Effectively none without a CRM — see above.
audit-my-automations.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it IS the skill. It supplies the only data the skill consumes: list_automations, the per-automation detail (embedded automations_triggers/automations_actions, dedup_enabled, max_executions_per_day), and the automations/:id/runs run log that powers every freshness/error/skip flag. It also receives the write-backs that apply the fixes. With no CRM connected the skill has no input and no target to act on, so it lives entirely behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section.

audit-my-data.current_function: A read-only data-hygiene audit. Runs two TrustPager-backed scripts (find-gaps.py, audit-contacts.py) that pull live opportunities, tasks, and contacts via the TrustPager API, then detects: opportunities with no contact/value/stage/owner, overdue and undated tasks, missing/malformed emails, likely-duplicate contacts (same email, or same name+company), dormant records (365d+ no activity, no open opp), and orphan contacts. Presents a worst-first fix checklist ranked by cost, then offers safe mechanical fixes one at a time with approval (assign owner, set value, archive dormant/orphan) and refuses to merge/delete without named confirmation. All reads go through the CRM; all Step-3 fixes are TrustPager MCP writes (update_opportunity, archive contact).
audit-my-data.standalone_value: The core value is generic data-quality reasoning, not a CRM operation: scan rows of contacts/deals/tasks, flag missing or malformed fields (no email, bad email, no value/owner/stage, no due date), detect likely duplicates (same email, or same name+company), surface dormant and orphan records, then rank the findings worst-first and hand the owner a prioritized fix checklist. None of that detection logic needs a live CRM — it is row-by-row gap/dedup analysis plus a presentation pattern. Point it at the owner's exported contact/deal/task spreadsheet (CSV or XLSX export from their existing tool, a contacts export, or a pasted list) and it still delivers a meaningful minute-one win: 'these 4 deals have no value, these 2 emails are duplicates, these 12 contacts have no email.' A standalone general-purpose version would read those rows from a file, apply the same checks, and output the same worst-first report; the only thing it can't do without a writable system is the optional auto-fix step, which it can instead emit as a marked-up checklist for the owner to apply by hand.
audit-my-data.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected the skill pulls the live workspace directly (no manual export needed), always audits current data, can use the operator's real pipeline/stage/field names, detects dormancy from true last_activity_at and open-opportunity counts rather than a static export, and — most importantly — closes the loop: instead of just listing fixes, it APPLIES the safe ones in place (assign an unowned opportunity, set a missing value, archive a dormant/orphan contact, dedupe with named confirmation) one at a time with approval. So TrustPager turns a read-only 'here's the mess' report into a live 'here's the mess and I just cleaned it' workflow.

automate-this.current_function: Turns a plain-English "WHEN X happens, DO Y" rule into a live TrustPager automation: discovers the workspace's available triggers, conditions, and action types; maps the rule to those primitives; builds the automation disabled; tests actions against sample data (email variable rendering, tagging, webhook bodies); sets safety dials (dedup, max executions/day); then enables it. Handles multi-trigger OR-match entry points, flags overlap with existing automations, and forks timed series off to the nurture-queue skill.
automate-this.standalone_value: The skill's core output is a running automation, which requires an automation engine to deploy into. Strip TrustPager and there is no runtime to create the trigger, schedule the actions, send the emails/SMS, or enforce dedup — the entire build/test/enable loop (create_automation, add_automation_action, add_automation_trigger, execute_automation_action, enable_automation) and the fetch.py discovery (live trigger schemas, action-type config schemas, existing-automation overlap check) collapse without the CRM. The only thing that survives is the design conversation — phrasing the rule, spotting that two entry points should be one automation with OR-match triggers, and recognizing when something is really a timed nurture queue. That reasoning is real but purely advisory with no platform to act on; it produces a spec, not a working automation, so it is not a standalone minute-one win. The value here genuinely IS a CRM/automation-platform operation, so it belongs behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section rather than polluting the general floor.
automate-this.tp_enhancement: N/A — this IS the TrustPager-native operation. TrustPager is the automation engine the whole skill targets: it supplies the trigger catalog and per-trigger {{variable}} schemas, the action-type config schemas, the existing-automation registry for overlap detection, the disabled-build + execute-test + enable workflow, the dedup/rate-limit safety dials, and the webhook/stage-automation wiring. Without it the skill has no engine to build into; with it, the skill delivers its full value of standing up a real, tested, running automation.

brand-my-workspace.current_function: Points at the user's public website, detects brand colours, fonts, name, logo and favicons, writes brand/brand.json + drops brand/logo.png, then runs tools/sync-brand.py to push the new assets into every BOS studio's public/ folder in one shot. The single theming touchpoint for all studios (thumbnails, CTAs, etc.).
brand-my-workspace.standalone_value: Delivers full value with zero CRM connected. The entire flow runs on a public URL (WebFetch/curl) plus pure reasoning to derive colour variants/gradients, and writes only local files (brand/brand.json, logo.png, favicons) consumed by the local tools/sync-brand.py. Any small-business owner who points it at their website — or just pastes their hex colours and drops a logo — gets every BOS studio rebranded to their identity. No fetch.py, no TrustPager tool call, no CRM data appears anywhere in the skill. This is a genuine minute-one win.
brand-my-workspace.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the skill could skip the website-scraping/guesswork entirely by pulling the workspace's already-configured brand assets — primary/accent colours, logo, business name and tagline — straight from the CRM's company/branding settings (e.g. get_our_company / get_crm_settings / company profile). That gives authoritative, exact brand values instead of best-effort detection from HTML, and keeps BOS studios automatically in sync with the brand the owner already maintains in TrustPager. It deepens accuracy but is never required: the standalone web-fetch / owner-paste path stands on its own.

build-brand-strategy.current_function: Authors the five canonical brand-strategy docs (positioning.md, icp.yaml, voice.md, value-props.yaml, content-pillars.yaml) by reading a local customer-voice-synthesis.md file plus the marketing-strategy-method knowledge doc, then writing the strategy docs into a local marketing-strategy/<Brand>/ folder. Every claim is anchored to a verbatim customer quote pulled from the synthesis. Pure reasoning over local files — no API or CRM calls.
build-brand-strategy.standalone_value: Delivers a complete, evidence-anchored brand-strategy pack (positioning, ICP, voice, value props, content pillars) for any business owner with zero tools connected. It reads a local synthesis file and writes local docs through reasoning alone — there is no fetch.py and no MCP/TrustPager call anywhere in the skill. The only input is a customer-voice-synthesis.md produced by the upstream general-purpose build-customer-voice skill (itself local-file based), so the entire chain runs offline on the owner's machine. This is a high-value minute-one deliverable: it turns raw customer language into a usable strategy foundation that normally costs an agency thousands.
build-brand-strategy.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not required and not used today. When connected, it can supply richer real customer evidence to feed the upstream synthesis (actual contact/company records, deal histories, logged call transcripts, won/lost reasons), making the quotes and ICP signals deeper and more current than what an owner pastes manually. The finished strategy docs could also be pushed into TrustPager as a knowledge base or AI-agent briefing, and the ICP/value-props could seed pipeline tagging or auto-queue messaging — but all of that is downstream enrichment, not a prerequisite for the skill to produce its full output.

build-customer-voice.current_function: Pulls >=5-minute call and meeting transcripts (via tools/dump-transcripts.py hitting the TrustPager transcripts API), reads every one verbatim, filters out the host/operator voice, and synthesises the customer's actual language into a 10-section voice-of-customer Markdown file (who's on the calls, pain in their words, jobs-to-be-done, objections, competing tools, buying moments, vocabulary list, who-it's-not-for, top-10 quotes, industry patterns). This file is the evidence foundation every downstream marketing artefact (brand voice, ICP, positioning, value props, nurture sequences) is authored from.
build-customer-voice.standalone_value: The irreplaceable value is the synthesis reasoning, not the data fetch. Steps 2-4 (read every transcript end-to-end, filter the host's voice, cluster pain into verbatim themes, mine the vocabulary list, surface buying moments and disqualifiers, rank the top-10 quotes) are pure language analysis over a corpus of conversation text. The TrustPager call only supplies that corpus. Swap the source and the engine is identical: a business owner with no CRM can drop transcripts exported from any notetaker/dialer (Otter, Fathom, Fireflies, Zoom, Gong) or a CSV of call notes into a local folder, and Claude produces the same canonical customer-voice synthesis. The 10-section template, host-filtering rule, verbatim-quote discipline, and 'don't invent themes' guardrails are all platform-agnostic. This is a genuine minute-of-value-after-you-have-a-few-calls win, just not a zero-tools win since it requires real conversation text to exist somewhere.
build-customer-voice.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, tools/dump-transcripts.py auto-harvests the corpus end-to-end: it pages the transcripts API for transcription_status=complete records (Recall AI Notetaker meetings + Retell voice-agent calls), filters by >=5min duration, splits into calls/ and meetings/ buckets, strips WebVTT timestamps to clean Markdown, and writes YAML frontmatter that links each transcript to its CRM deal and contact. So TrustPager removes all manual exporting/collation, keeps the corpus current as new calls land, and enriches each quote with who-they-are context (linked deal/contact, industry, business name) that a loose folder of files would lack — making the 'Who's actually on these calls' and footnoted-attribution sections far richer than a standalone export allows.

build-document.current_function: Plans a reusable signing-document template (proposal, service agreement, contract, consent form) by interviewing the operator about document type, signer order, and fixed-vs-variable copy — optionally reverse-engineering an existing PDF/Word sample — then creates it in TrustPager as an ordered set of sections with merge fields and signer-input blocks (create_document_template + add_document_section + reorder_document_sections), reads it back, and previews the resolved PDF against a test opportunity. Explicitly does NOT send (that's send-for-signing).
build-document.standalone_value: A business owner with no tools connected gets an interview-driven, properly structured reusable contract/proposal/agreement draft on a local file, with merge placeholders and per-signer signature blocks marked — useful and sendable manually, just without automatic data-fill or tracked e-signing.
build-document.tp_enhancement: TrustPager turns the plan into a live reusable template with auto-resolving merge fields, recipient-fillable signer inputs on a hosted page, render-to-preview against a real opportunity, and a clean handoff to tracked sending/linting/radar.

build-knowledge-base-from-docs.current_function: Converts a business's documents (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML) to Markdown via the local MarkItDown tool, splits them into focused knowledge entries (one per topic/policy/FAQ with a clear title), shows the operator the proposed entry plan for confirmation, then loads the entries into TrustPager AI Knowledge (create_knowledge / ingest_knowledge_base_text) so the in-app assistant and voice agents answer from the client's real documents.
build-knowledge-base-from-docs.standalone_value: The valuable work here is the convert-and-structure pipeline, and it runs entirely on local files with no CRM. Step 1 uses the bundled tools/markitdown_convert.py to turn any PDF/Word/slides/Excel/HTML into clean Markdown; Step 2 uses pure reasoning to split that into focused, well-titled knowledge entries in the customer's own words, flagging empty/image-only conversions and refusing to invent or merge content. A business owner with nothing connected gets a real deliverable: their messy folder of policy/FAQ/product/process docs turned into an organized, de-duplicated set of answerable Q&A-style entries written to local Markdown files, directly reusable in any chatbot, help center, or internal wiki. Only the final write target (Steps 3-4) is TrustPager-specific; swap it for a local /knowledge folder or Markdown/JSON file and the core value lands standalone.
build-knowledge-base-from-docs.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the structured entries load directly into TrustPager AI Knowledge via create_knowledge / ingest_knowledge_base_text, batched with streamed progress and the approval queue respected (202 = queued). Each entry is tagged with its source document for traceability and easy refresh when a policy changes. The loaded knowledge becomes live: the in-app assistant and voice agents immediately answer customers from the business's real documents, turning a static owner-managed file into an operational, auto-answering knowledge layer wired into the CRM's AI surfaces.

build-spreadsheet.current_function: Builds one of two TrustPager spreadsheet types. Path A (workspace) creates a CRM-sourced spreadsheet via create_spreadsheet, adds opportunity/custom-field columns, builds per-period views with running sum totals on live data, and offers a scheduled rolling auto-create of next period's view. Path B (standalone) builds a self-contained sheet not bound to the CRM — from scratch off owner-described columns, from a spreadsheet template, or by importing an existing Excel/CSV (converted locally via tools/markitdown_convert.py, then bulk_append_spreadsheet_rows) — and adds formulas/totals (e.g. amount x rate, sums) after confirming the logic in plain language.
build-spreadsheet.standalone_value: The skill's Path B is already designed to be CRM-independent ("holds its own data... isn't bound to the CRM"). The durable core value is turning either a plain-language description or a messy real-world Excel/CSV into a structured, calculating spreadsheet: pick columns and types, import existing rows, and apply formulas/totals with the logic confirmed in plain language first. A business owner with nothing connected can hand over a downloaded export or describe a commission calculator / planner / tracker and get a working sheet — a genuine minute-one win. Only Path A (live-from-CRM totals and the rolling auto-create automation) depends on the CRM; the standalone build does not. The Excel/CSV import path notably already routes through a LOCAL tool (tools/markitdown_convert.py), not TrustPager, so the conversion step is platform-agnostic today.
build-spreadsheet.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the skill unlocks Path A: the spreadsheet sources LIVE from the CRM (opportunities + custom fields), auto-creates per-period views that sum real settlement/pipeline data and stay current as records change, and can offer a scheduled automation that rolls next month's view forward automatically. TrustPager also gives the standalone sheet a hosted home in the workspace (rather than a local file), shareable views, and access to spreadsheet templates. The general-purpose version delivers the build/import/calculate value on local files; TrustPager turns it into a living, CRM-fed reporting surface and adds the rolling automation no local file can match.

build-work-order-process.current_function: Sets up the work-order PROCESS layer inside TrustPager: interviews the owner about their job workflow, reads the existing board (list_work_order_statuses / list_work_order_fields) to avoid duplicates, then creates the statuses (create_work_order_status + reorder_work_order_statuses) and custom fields (create_work_order_field) jobs will be tracked against. Closes by offering to raise the first work order against a deal_product_id and handing off to the radar/automation skills.
build-work-order-process.standalone_value: The skill's deliverable is a configured work-order board living inside the CRM — statuses and custom fields created as TrustPager records via create_work_order_status / create_work_order_field, with reorder calls to set the sequence. These records only mean something because work orders later attach to a deal_product_id (a line item on an opportunity that exists only in the CRM), move through the live statuses, and surface to customers on a PIN-protected portal that fires work_order_opened. Strip TrustPager and there is no board to read, nothing to create the statuses/fields ON, and no jobs/products/portal for them to govern — a status list written to a local markdown file is inert (you cannot move a job across it, capture a field on it, or show a customer progress). The upstream workflow-design conversation (Step 1: pick 4-6 tight stages, decide what to record per job) is platform-agnostic reasoning, but on its own it is a different, much lighter skill, not the value this skill ships. As written, the skill collapses to nothing operational without the CRM.
build-work-order-process.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The skill exists to build the work-order process objects (statuses + fields) inside the TrustPager workspace and connect them to the broader fulfilment machinery: deal products to attach work orders to, the customer portal, send_work_status updates, and work_order_opened automation triggers. Every create/read/reorder call targets the live CRM. This belongs behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section. If a general-purpose spin-off were ever wanted, it would be a separate, narrower skill that only drafts a recommended job-status workflow + field schema into local files (data source: dictation / business-profile) and stops short of building anything — but that is not this skill.

compare-documents.current_function: Converts two documents (PDF, Word, etc.) to Markdown via the local tools/markitdown_convert.py tool, then reports the meaningful differences in plain language — grouped Added / Removed / Changed — leading with money, dates, obligations, and parties, and ending with a one-line net-effect summary. Built for comparing contract versions, revised quotes, and updated terms/policies.
compare-documents.standalone_value: Delivers a complete, meaningful win with zero tools connected. The owner drops two file versions (Quote-v1.pdf and Quote-v2.pdf, an old and revised contract, last month's vs this month's policy) and gets a clean human-readable answer to the constant question "what actually changed?" — figures shown old → new, new clauses flagged, removed terms called out — instead of squinting through a character-level diff or re-reading both PDFs. The entire pipeline is local: MarkItDown conversion of the files plus model reasoning over the two Markdown outputs. No CRM, no account, no network data source is involved at any step. This is a pure minute-one floor capability.
compare-documents.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the two versions to compare can be pulled directly from the CRM instead of the owner hunting for files — e.g. fetch an opportunity's attached documents/files (list_opportunity_documents / list_opportunity_files / download_file) or two revisions of a signing envelope/quote, compare them, and write the plain-language change summary back as a note on the deal (add_note / add_opportunity_notepad). That closes the loop (compare → record on the record) but the core compare-and-report value lands fully without any of it.

delegate-this-work.current_function: Turns a verbal delegation ("Sarah should prep the Acme demo by Friday") into a tracked hand-off: confirms what/who/when/priority, checks the operator's role permits delegating, creates the task in TrustPager assigned to the named team member (linked to the opportunity/contact), notifies the assignee with a link, sets a manager follow-up task on the due date to verify completion, and journals who-assigned-what-to-whom.
delegate-this-work.standalone_value: The core value is making delegation "land and get followed up" — and that mechanism is mostly reasoning + record-keeping, not inherently a CRM operation. Standalone, the skill can still: (1) capture the four things (what, who, when, priority) from the operator's ask; (2) resolve "who" against the team roster in the business profile / team-standards file; (3) enforce the role-based permission check (manager/owner/ops may delegate) from that same profile; (4) draft the assignee notification in the team voice; and (5) record the delegation AND a paired manager follow-up reminder to a local delegation log or tasks file (e.g. a markdown/CSV task list). The follow-up reminder — "the bit that stops delegations vanishing," which the skill itself calls the point — works entirely from a local file plus the owner's own calendar/reminders. So a business owner with nothing connected still gets a tracked, accountable hand-off with a built-in verification step. What it loses standalone is the live wiring (auto-assigning to a real user record, auto-linking to the opportunity, surfacing on the contact, real automated send), but the delegation discipline itself survives the data-source swap.
delegate-this-work.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the delegation stops being a logged note and becomes a real, wired operation: create_task assigns the work to the assignee's actual user id with due_date/priority and links it to the live opportunity_id/contact_id so it surfaces on the record; the assignee gets a genuine SMS/email send with a working task link via the CRM's comms; the manager follow-up becomes a real assigned task (not just a personal reminder) that lives in the same task system; and the team roster + role table resolve against actual workspace users instead of a static profile file. TrustPager also enforces the approval gate (HTTP 202 queued) and auto-journals the write, giving real accountability and an audit trail that a local file can only approximate.

design-nurture-sequence.current_function: Designs a multi-step email nurture sequence in the operator's voice: confirms sequence shape (audience, trigger, goal, stages/delays), maps a help-center video to each stage anchored to a verbatim customer pain, drafts subject + HTML body per email following a canonical shape, and presents all drafts in chat for review. Explicitly a design-only skill that does NOT write to the live auto queue (handoff to wire-nurture-sequence for that).
design-nurture-sequence.standalone_value: The core deliverable is authored email copy produced by pure reasoning over local files, not a CRM operation. It reads the operator's voice.md, value-props.yaml, content-pillars.yaml, and a customer-voice synthesis, then drafts a full multi-step sequence — subject lines, HTML bodies, per-email pain anchors, cadence — entirely in chat for review. The two TrustPager touchpoints are non-essential to that value: (1) confirming queue stages/delays via dump-crm-bundle.py, which the owner could just describe ("Day 0, 2, 4, 6"), and (2) listing help-center videos via a public curl endpoint, which can be swapped for any content list the owner pastes. Strip the CRM entirely and you still get a complete, voice-matched, pain-anchored nurture sequence ready to copy into any email tool (Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, Gmail). Nothing is written anywhere — the output is markdown drafts, so it lands standalone.
design-nurture-sequence.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the skill auto-discovers the real auto-queue stages and delays (so the cadence matches an actual queue instead of a guessed default), pulls the canonical TrustPager help-center video library to map a precise concern-cutting video to each stage, and hands off cleanly to wire-nurture-sequence to push the approved drafts straight into the live auto queue via MCP — closing the loop from design to deployment without copy-paste. Standalone it stops at finished drafts; connected it becomes design-to-live in one flow.

draft-reply.current_function: Drafts a tone-matched reply to an inbound email or SMS. Phase 1 uses TrustPager fetch.py to surface unanswered inbound messages (ranked by open-opportunity then recency); phase 2 reads the inbound, drafts the reply (acknowledge-then-answer, match tone, answer what was actually asked, one next step, no fake enthusiasm, never invent facts), shows it for approval, then sends via reply_to_email (threaded) or send_sms.
draft-reply.standalone_value: The core value — turning a received message into a well-judged reply — is pure reasoning over the inbound text and needs no CRM. The skill is already built to run standalone: SKILL.md line 31 explicitly says "If the user pastes a message directly (not from the JSON), use that paste as the source-of-truth and skip the fetch." Given a pasted or dictated inbound, the skill still delivers its full reasoning payload: identify what they're actually asking, read the emotional register, preserve specific details (names, dates, dollar amounts), acknowledge-before-answering, tone-match, address multi-question emails in the same structure, end with one next step, ban fake enthusiasm, and never invent facts. A standalone owner pastes the email/SMS they received and copies the approved draft into their own mail or phone app — reply quality is identical. This is not a live CRM operation, so it is extractable rather than trustpager_native: only the inbox-discovery and the threaded auto-send depend on the CRM, and both have clean standalone substitutes.
draft-reply.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, fetch.py removes the need to find the message manually: it sweeps every inbound email thread + SMS conversation in the window with no reply and ranks them (open-opportunity senders first, then recency), so the owner is shown the top 3-5 to pick from instead of pasting. On send, reply_to_email preserves the email thread (the skill warns send_email would break threading) and keeps the inbound CC list intact, send_sms delivers the SMS in-platform, and the reply is logged against the linked opportunity/contact record. Pulled contact context (open deal, prior thread) also lets the draft reference history the owner did not paste. None of this is required to get a great reply — it deepens an already-useful standalone skill.

email-me-a-report.current_function: Turns a TrustPager report dashboard into a recurring, self-delivering email digest: picks or builds a dashboard from CRM report sources (opportunities, tasks, invoices), proves the card queries with query_report, then wires a send_report_email action onto an auto_schedule cron so it renders per-recipient and emails chosen inboxes server-side on a schedule (e.g. 7am weekdays) with no app open. fetch.py lists existing dashboards, available report sources, and running auto-schedules so it doesn't duplicate.
email-me-a-report.standalone_value: n/a — the core value is a CRM/platform operation that collapses without TrustPager. The defining promise is unattended, recurring, server-side delivery: a dashboard that renders itself per-recipient and emails chosen inboxes on a cron with nothing open. Every load-bearing piece is a hosted-platform entity — report_dashboard, report_card, query_report, the send_report_email action, and the auto_schedule cron — and the report's raw material is live CRM data (opportunities/tasks/invoices via report sources). A standalone Claude Code session is not a persistent server: it cannot fire a cron at 7am or send email server-side while no app is running, so there is no local-files/paste/business-profile substitute that reproduces the skill's actual value. The only sliver that could run standalone — compute numbers from a pasted CSV and draft one email now — is a different, one-off skill, and SKILL.md explicitly routes that case away ("wants the numbers right now, once... don't build a schedule"). Calling this extractable would over-claim and break the works-for-anyone floor.
email-me-a-report.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. It supplies the reportable data sources, the dashboard/card builder and query engine, the per-recipient render-and-send action, and the server-side cron scheduler that makes the digest arrive on its own. This skill lives behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section; with no CRM connected there is nothing to schedule, render, or send unattended.

extract-document.current_function: Converts any document (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, image/scan, HTML, CSV, JSON, ZIP) to Markdown via the local MarkItDown wrapper (tools/markitdown_convert.py), then performs the extraction the operator asked for: answer a question / summarise, pull named fields as a clean list/table, or map extracted fields onto a named TrustPager CRM opportunity/contact (write-after-confirm, respecting the approval queue).
extract-document.standalone_value: The skill's core value — turn a file the owner has on disk into usable data — lands with zero tools connected. Two of its three modes (answer/summarise a document, pull named fields like applicant name/income/loan amount) run entirely on a locally converted Markdown file and require nothing external. The conversion engine is the offline, open-source MarkItDown tool invoked via tools/markitdown_convert.py, with no CRM call. The SKILL even self-describes as "the general 'read a document and do something with it' skill." Only the optional third mode (map onto a CRM record) touches TrustPager, and it is a final write step, not the value itself. This is a genuine minute-one win for any owner with a PDF/scan/spreadsheet.
extract-document.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the extracted fields stop being a one-off list and get written into the live CRM: each named field (applicant, income, loan amount, property) is matched to the real workspace field on a specific opportunity/contact, shown as a proposed mapping for confirmation, then committed (honouring the 202 approval-queue path). So a mortgage broker can drop in an ANZ statement and have the deal record populated, not just read back the numbers. Without TP the owner gets the clean extracted values to use however they like (paste into their own sheet, file, or another tool); with TP the same extraction becomes structured data living on the customer record.

follow-up-radar.current_function: Surfaces active opportunities that have gone quiet (no activity in N+ days, no scheduled next-action), ranks them by deal value x days-silent, drafts a personalised re-engagement message per deal (channel chosen by available contact + unsubscribe flags), and presents each draft for per-item operator approval. On approval it sends via TrustPager send_sms/send_email and logs an add_note so the next sweep skips it. Data is pulled entirely from TrustPager via fetch.py (opportunities + enriched contacts).
follow-up-radar.standalone_value: The real value is the reasoning, not the CRM write: detecting which deals have gone silent, prioritising them (value x days-quiet, with an unpriced-deal floor so stale-but-unpriced leads don't vanish), and drafting a specific, personalised, non-templated re-engagement message for each with a concrete next-step ask. None of that requires a live CRM. Give the skill a list of deals with name, stage, value, last-contacted date and contact details and it can do the whole job: triage the backlog, rank it, and hand back N ready-to-send drafts in minutes. A standalone owner reviews each draft and sends it from their own phone or email - the minute-one win ("here are the 10 deals you forgot about, message ready for each") fully lands without TrustPager.
follow-up-radar.tp_enhancement: TrustPager auto-detects the silent set live (computes days_silent from updated_at, respects scheduled next_action_date, filters won/lost/cancelled stages) so the owner never has to assemble or paste a deal list - the radar just runs. It enriches each top deal with current contact details and email/SMS unsubscribe flags so channel choice and compliance are automatic. On approval it actually sends via send_sms/send_email and writes an add_note back to the opportunity, which suppresses that deal from the next sweep - closing the loop so the radar self-maintains. Without TrustPager the owner supplies the export and sends manually; with it, detection, sending, and suppression are all automated.

form-radar.current_function: Pulls every form submission from the CRM and turns it into a sent → opened → completed funnel, surfacing two follow-up buckets — recipients who opened/started a form but never submitted (nudge) and forms sent but never opened that are going stale (chase/resend) — oldest-first, plus a recently-completed count. Offers approval-gated resend/void actions and hands off to /automate-this on the form_opened trigger.
form-radar.standalone_value: Minimal standalone value. The skill's core differentiator is the engagement lifecycle — distinguishing "sent but never opened" from "opened but didn't finish" from "completed." Those open/start/abandon signals are telemetry that only a live form-delivery and tracking system (the CRM) can produce; an owner with nothing connected has no way to know a recipient viewed a form without submitting it. The follow-up actions (resend_form_submission, void_form_submission) and the form_opened automation trigger are all live CRM/form-platform operations. Strip the CRM and you are left with "a flat list of forms I think I sent and who hasn't replied" — which is weaker than, and largely subsumed by, general follow-up/outstanding-item reasoning. The thing that makes Form Radar *Form Radar* collapses without the form-tracking backend.
form-radar.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. It supplies the only viable data source (forms/submissions via list_form_submissions) carrying the per-recipient lifecycle status (viewed/opened/in_progress/completed/expired/voided) and timestamps that the funnel and both follow-up buckets are computed from. It also provides every downstream action the skill offers: resend_form_submission, void_form_submission, auto-archiving completed-form PDFs to opportunities, and wiring the form_opened automation trigger. The value IS a CRM/form-tracking operation, so this skill lives behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section rather than in the general floor.

import-from-anywhere.current_function: Takes data pasted in any shape (CSV/TSV, OCR'd screenshot text, PDF/Word/Excel tables converted via MarkItDown, copy-pasted email lists, free-text "people I met" lists) and turns it into clean structured records. It detects the data shape, extracts fields, normalizes phones to E.164, builds a preview table, flags issues (missing emails, OCR errors, unparseable rows), runs dedup against existing records, asks for confirmation, then bulk-writes. Today the dedup baseline is built by fetch.py pulling existing contacts/companies/open opportunities from TrustPager, and the final write targets TrustPager via bulk_create_contacts / bulk_create_opportunities / bulk_create_companies (or bulk_append_spreadsheet_rows for a sheet dump).
import-from-anywhere.standalone_value: A small-business owner drowning in messy contact data — a conference badge-scan export, a screenshot of a phone contact list, a supplier's CSV, a forwarded email of leads — pastes it and gets back a clean, deduplicated, phone-normalized, field-mapped table with issues flagged (missing emails, OCR typos, half-records) and a preview to confirm before anything is written. Delivered as a local CSV/JSON/spreadsheet, that is a genuine standalone "clean up and structure my contact mess" win with zero tools connected.
import-from-anywhere.tp_enhancement: TrustPager turns the local clean-up into a populate-my-CRM action: live cross-workspace dedup against existing contacts/companies/open deals, direct bulk-create of the records with the original paste saved as a traceable source note, and opportunities placed onto a chosen pipeline and stage.

lead-triage.current_function: Pulls every new inbound lead from the last N hours across TrustPager sources (form submissions, inbound email threads, inbound SMS, recently-created open opportunities), computes a 0-100 fit score from contact completeness + message length + source quality, classifies each into fast-track / nurture / cold / disqualify (with spam heuristics), then drafts a personalized first-touch message per lead and sends it per-lead with approval. Optionally creates the opportunity first and marks disqualified leads "lost".
lead-triage.standalone_value: The genuine value is the triage brain, not the CRM plumbing: scoring leads by fit, sorting who to call first, classifying into fast-track/nurture/cold/disqualify, catching spam patterns (SEO/web-design/partnership/backlink solicitations), and drafting a personalized first response that references something concrete from each enquiry. All of that is pure reasoning over a list of lead records — score(), category(), the spam signals, and the drafting guidance in SKILL.md never touch TrustPager. A solo owner who pastes in last night's contact-form submissions, forwards a handful of inbound emails, or hands over a leads CSV gets the same minute-one win: a ranked, categorized list with a ready-to-send reply for each. Only the data-pull step (fetch.py) and the send/create-opportunity/mark-lost actions are CRM-bound, and those are swappable (read the source, owner copies the drafted reply into their own inbox).
lead-triage.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected it (1) auto-discovers leads across all inbound channels — form submissions, email threads, SMS conversations, and new open opportunities — instead of the owner gathering them by hand; (2) enriches each lead with linked contact/company records to sharpen the fit score; (3) lets fast-track leads be pushed straight into the live pipeline via create_opportunity; (4) sends the approved reply on the lead's own channel via send_email/send_sms; and (5) marks disqualified leads "lost" with a reason for later review. It turns a paste-and-reason workout into a one-command sweep-score-respond loop, but none of those are required to get the triage value.

learn-my-business.current_function: Reads the operator's live TrustPager workspace (via fetch.py: pipelines+stages, products+prices, company profile/brand, CRM settings lead sources/types/reasons, rough record counts), matches the business to a section in knowledge/industry-notes.md, then writes a filled CLAUDE.md profile into the operator's project folder using templates/CLAUDE.md as the structure. It is the setup front door that replaces hand-filling a template, so Claude starts every session knowing the business.
learn-my-business.standalone_value: The deliverable is a written CLAUDE.md business-context profile (business name/city, products + prices, pipeline stages, lead sources, ideal customer/tone, plus confirmed industry gotchas). That artifact is just structured business knowledge — its value does not depend on a CRM existing. With nothing connected, Claude can produce the same file by interviewing the owner (a handful of short questions about their products, pipeline stages, and how they want to sound), folding in the matched industry-notes.md gotchas (pure reasoning, no tools), and filling the same templates/CLAUDE.md scaffold. The SKILL already bakes in this path: it instructs Claude to "ask the operator one short question rather than guessing" for any unavailable section, and the template itself offers a manual fill ("edit anything in <<< ... >>>"). So a general-purpose version ships cleanly: same template, same industry knowledge base, owner-described inputs instead of an API digest. The minute-one win (Claude knowing your business going forward) still lands. It is not general_floor because, as written, Step 1 is an API read and the whole flow is framed around auto-reading the live workspace; the zero-tools path requires swapping the data source to an owner interview/paste.
learn-my-business.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, fetch.py reads the real workspace shape — exact pipeline names and stage order, real product names/prices/currency, company profile + brand color, CRM settings (lead sources, opportunity types, won/lost reasons), and rough record counts — so the CLAUDE.md is filled from ground truth instead of the owner's recollection. That removes the interview burden, eliminates guessing/typos in stage and product names (the hard rule "use the operator's exact stage and product names as the workspace spells them" only holds with a live read), keeps the file accurate on re-run as the workspace evolves, and lets the written profile correctly point to TrustPager as the source of truth. TrustPager turns a "describe your business to me" exercise into a one-command "I already read it, here's your file" — deeper and lower-effort, but not required for the core value.

lint-document.current_function: Read-only pre-flight linter for a document/signing template. Loads the template via TrustPager (list_document_templates -> get_document_template) and walks every section and signer to catch client-facing mistakes before the first send: a signer with no signature/initials input, an orphan signature block assigned to a non-signer, broken/malformed {{merge_field}} tokens, an empty template (FAILS); plus likely-blank merge fields, leftover placeholder text (Lorem ipsum/TODO/[INSERT]/XXXX), missing date-next-to-signature, and missing required disclaimers (WARNINGS). Never edits — reports fails-first then warnings and routes every fix to /build-document, ending with a clean hand-off to /send-for-signing.
lint-document.standalone_value: The core value is document QA by structural reasoning, not a CRM operation. Every check — signer-without-input, orphan signature block, malformed/unclosed {{merge_field}} tokens, leftover placeholder text, missing date field, missing required disclaimer — can be performed on a document the owner already has on disk or pastes in: a DOCX/Markdown contract, an exported signing template, or pasted template text with {{tokens}}. A solo owner about to email a quote or agreement gets a real minute-one win: "your guarantor has nothing to sign and {{contact.fulname}} is misspelled — fix these two before you send." No account, no connection required. It is bucketed extractable (not general_floor) only because today it has a hard TrustPager dependency for the data source (it calls list/get_document_template and has no local-file path yet); the value lands standalone the moment we swap the loader to read a local file or pasted text.
lint-document.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the skill pulls the live document/signing template structure directly (sections, signer set, signature/initials inputs) instead of asking the owner to locate or paste a file, so it can verify the actual signer roster and input assignments rather than inferring them. It can also validate merge tokens against the real field catalog — confirming {{contact.full_name}} or {{deal.value}} are genuine field paths and flagging ones usually blank on that specific workspace's deals — which a standalone version can only heuristically guess. And because the template lives in TrustPager, the report's fix hand-offs (/build-document) and clean-bill hand-off (/send-for-signing) become one-click next steps on the same live template.

lint-form.current_function: A read-only pre-flight linter for a TrustPager form template. Loads the template + fields via get_form_template / list_form_fields, then checks for orphan data fields (collects data but not wired to a CRM variable -> FAIL), label vs wiring mismatches (FAIL), empty templates and broken/zero-option select sets (FAIL), and warns on unset-required fields, leftover placeholder text, duplicate labels, and unrouted file uploads. Reports fails-first and routes fixes to /build-form and /wire-form. Edits nothing.
lint-form.standalone_value: A general-purpose form-readiness linter delivers real value with no CRM connected. Given a form definition the owner already has, it catches the silent ship-breakers: empty templates, select/radio sets with zero options, fields missing a required flag, leftover placeholder text ("Lorem ipsum", "TODO", "test field", "[label]"), and duplicate labels that confuse the record/PDF. The two CRM-flavoured checks generalize cleanly: "orphan field" becomes "field with no mapped destination" and "label vs wiring mismatch" becomes "label disagrees with its mapped column/field" — both checkable against any declared destination schema (a spreadsheet header row, a pasted field-to-column map, the business profile's record fields). Linting is data-source-agnostic by nature: it only needs the form spec plus the intended destination fields, neither of which has to come from TrustPager.
lint-form.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the linter reads the actual live template and field wiring via get_form_template / list_form_fields, so "orphan" and "label vs wiring mismatch" are checked against real CRM variables (contact.email, deal.value, custom fields) instead of an owner-declared destination map — no manual mapping needed and zero drift between what's checked and what ships. It can also route each fix straight into the connected /build-form and /wire-form steps and confirm the form is ready to send via send_form or collect via intake, closing the loop end to end.

lint-nurture-sequence.current_function:
A deterministic style/quality gate that lints a nurture email sequence against house style. Per email it checks subject presence/length, greeting, HTML

structure, that at least one link exists, that a clickable TEXT CTA appears ABOVE the first image (the image-blocked-client gap), a consistent sign-off, positively-framed subject, and no em dash. Across the set it flags MIXED cta-above-image as a hard FAIL, plus inconsistent sign-offs and P.S. presence. It only reports and routes fixes (to design-/wire-nurture-sequence); it never edits anything. Two input paths exist today: --queue (pull each step's send-action email from a live TrustPager auto queue via trustpager_api) and --drafts (read a local JSON array of {label, subject, body}).
lint-nurture-sequence.standalone_value: The entire value is a deterministic text analysis of email copy — the linting engine in tools/lint-sequence.py operates purely on subject/body strings and never needs the CRM to reason. The --drafts path ALREADY makes it standalone: an owner pastes or exports their sequence as a JSON array (or any tool that gives them the email drafts) and gets the full per-email + set-wide verdict. A solo operator drafting a welcome/onboarding drip in a doc, or pulling exported campaign HTML from Mailchimp/ActiveCampaign/ConvertKit, can run this and immediately learn which emails will silently underperform (no CTA above the image, drifting sign-offs, negative subjects) — a meaningful minute-one win with nothing connected. It is extractable rather than general_floor only because the shipped skill leads with a TrustPager queue id and the standalone path needs the drafts assembled into the expected JSON shape first (a light data-prep step), not because the logic depends on a CRM.
lint-nurture-sequence.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, the --queue path lints what is ACTUALLY deployed and running, not just drafts. It walks the live auto-queue steps in order, resolves each step's automation, finds the send-action (send_gmail_email / send_custom_email / send_marketing_email), and lints the real subject+body — so it catches DRIFT in a sequence already mailing real contacts (e.g. someone edited Day 14 and broke the CTA pattern). It also removes the manual data-prep entirely: no copy-paste, the queue id (from /nurture-health or dump-crm-bundle) is the only input, and it slots cleanly between design-nurture-sequence and wire-nurture-sequence as the pre-ship and post-deploy quality gate in one CRM-native loop.

log-this-call.current_function: After a customer call, resolves the person/opportunity in the CRM, walks the owner through a 4-question recap, then writes a structured note to the opportunity, moves the deal to the right pipeline stage, creates a task for the agreed next step, and notifies other assigned users — all via TrustPager tools (fetch.py reads contacts/deals/activities/tasks; add_note, move_opportunity_card, create_task, send_email write back).
log-this-call.standalone_value: Thin and degraded. With nothing connected, the only surviving fragment is the pure-reasoning part of Step 2: the agent could walk the owner through the 4 structured questions (discussed / their position / agreed / next contact) and format a clean recap. But that is the small tail of the skill, not its value. The skill's actual promise — the three things in its own opening lines — is "the CRM gets a useful recap, the opportunity moves to the right stage, the next step is scheduled, and the team is notified." Every one of those is a write against a live CRM: there is no contact to resolve, no open opportunity to move through a pipeline, no task to drop into the owner's queue, and no other assigned users to notify. fetch.py is entirely TrustPager reads (contacts -> deals -> activities -> tasks) and Steps 3-4 are entirely TrustPager writes (add_note, move_opportunity_card, create_task, send_email internal). Strip the CRM and the recap becomes an orphaned note with nowhere to live and nothing to advance — that is a different, far smaller product than "log this call into the system of record where the deal and the team live."
log-this-call.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The fetch resolves the caller against live contacts and assembles open opportunities, recent activities, and open tasks in one call so the agent picks the right deal without 3-5 manual lookups; the writes post the recap as a note on that opportunity, advance the pipeline stage, schedule the agreed next-step task, and fan a notification out to other assigned users on the deal. Without the connected workspace none of these targets exist, so the call-logging value collapses.

make-it-happen.current_function: A catch-all natural-language orchestration skill: the user describes an outcome in plain English and the skill figures out which TrustPager MCP tools to call, in what order, gating every destructive CRM operation behind explicit approval. Step 0 warms a TrustPager-specific discovery cache (AI instructions, trigger schemas, action types, existing automations) via fetch.py, which hits the TrustPager API directly. All discovery tools, the hard-block list, the existing-skill routing, and the HTTP 202 approval-queue handling are TrustPager CRM mechanisms.
make-it-happen.standalone_value: None as written. This skill is pure CRM orchestration glue — a dispatcher whose only job is translating a request into a sequence of live TrustPager tool calls. There is no local-file, pasted-data, or business-profile path: every step (discovery via mcp__trustpager__describe_resource/list_action_types, execution, the destructive hard-blocks like delete_contact / move opportunities / release_phone_number / disable_automation, and the approval queue) is a CRM operation against a connected workspace. The cached payload (trigger schemas, action types, automations) is meaningless without a CRM to act on. Strip TrustPager and nothing executable remains. A generic plain-English task router could conceptually be built standalone, but THIS skill is specifically the TrustPager command dispatcher and collapses without the connector.
make-it-happen.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The entire skill exists to drive the connected CRM: discover the available trigger/action/automation surface, route to the correct write tools, execute multi-step operations (tag + bulk-update + enrol in auto-queue, move deals, delete contacts), and respect the live approval queue (HTTP 202). Without a connected TrustPager workspace the skill has no tools to call and no outcome to deliver. It belongs entirely behind the optional connect-TrustPager section.

make-social-post.current_function: Designs and renders branded social-post PNGs (Instagram square/portrait, LinkedIn, X) from a headline-first "billboard" layout via a bundled local Vite + React + Puppeteer studio, with an optional one-command publish that uploads the rendered PNGs to the operator's TrustPager Files > Images > Social Posts folder.
make-social-post.standalone_value: The entire create-render loop runs offline against local files with nothing connected. The operator picks a format, supplies the one message/headline/accent word (Step 1), the design is written into the local studio/social/src/data/samples.json (Step 2), iterated in a local Vite dev server (Step 3), and rendered to a finished PNG via local Puppeteer + Chrome into studio/social/output/ (Step 4). That output PNG IS the deliverable — Step 5 publish is explicitly optional, and the hard rules say "If they'd rather post by hand, the PNG in studio/social/output/ is the deliverable." A business owner with zero TrustPager account gets a fully rendered, on-brand, multi-format social graphic at minute one. No fetch.py exists; the only code that touches TrustPager is the optional scripts/publish.js.
make-social-post.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, Step 5 (npm run publish) uploads the rendered PNG(s) straight into the operator's TrustPager Files > Images > Social Posts folder — auth resolving from $TRUSTPAGER_API_KEY or ~/.claude/bos.json — idempotently (skip-if-exists, --replace to overwrite, --all for the whole campaign). This turns a manual "save the PNG and upload it somewhere" step into a one-command path into the connected workspace's asset library, and could also pull brand palette/handle from the business profile to pre-fill the brief. None of this is required to get the finished graphic; it only removes the manual file-handling step.

make-thumbnail.current_function: Designs and renders a 1280x720 YouTube tutorial thumbnail using the bundled local Vite + React + Puppeteer "Thumbnail Studio" (studio/thumbnails/). Walks the operator through confirming a brief, picking one of 6 hero families, adding a design entry to samples.json, iterating live in the browser, quality-checking title/headline/hero/banned-framing rules distilled from 22+ iterations, then rendering a PNG via real Chrome (npm run shoot). An optional final step uploads the PNG to the operator's TrustPager Files > Images > Tutorial Thumbnails folder.
make-thumbnail.standalone_value: The entire design-and-render pipeline runs 100% locally and produces the actual deliverable with zero tools connected: a finished 1280x720 PNG written to studio/thumbnails/output/. Steps 1-4 (brief, hero selection, samples.json entry, live browser iteration, quality checks, puppeteer render) require nothing external — just the bundled studio and Node. The SKILL.md explicitly states "The shoot output in studio/thumbnails/output/ is the deliverable" and the operator can post that PNG manually to YouTube Studio. The embedded design methodology (headline-first layout, accent-word rule, 6 hero families, banned framings, YouTube title patterns) is pure local knowledge baked into the studio files and knowledge/youtube-thumbnail-method.md — no CRM data feeds the design. This is a genuine minute-one win for any business owner who wants tutorial/video thumbnails.
make-thumbnail.tp_enhancement: TrustPager only appears in the explicitly-optional Step 5: `npm run publish <design-key>` uploads the rendered PNG into the operator's own TrustPager workspace (Files > Images > Tutorial Thumbnails), with idempotent re-publish/rename/replace handling and bulk --all support. When connected, it removes the manual upload step and gives the thumbnails a managed home in the CRM's file library. The skill itself flags this as optional ("Publish is optional... skip publish") and auth degrades gracefully (env var or ~/.claude/bos.json). To make this truly platform-agnostic, the publish step should generalize to any destination (local folder, generic cloud storage, or another connected file tool) with TrustPager as one connector among several — but no code change is needed for the skill to already deliver full value without it.

missed-call-recovery.current_function: Pulls every missed inbound call from the last N hours out of the TrustPager phone call logs, enriches each with caller identity (contact lookup by phone), linked open opportunity + stage, and whether the call has already been returned, then ranks them (known caller with open opp > known caller > unknown) and drafts a per-call recovery SMS/email that is sent one-at-a-time with explicit approval via send_sms/send_email.
missed-call-recovery.standalone_value: Minimal as a standalone skill. The entire premise depends on a live feed of missed inbound calls plus the ability to detect whether each was already returned and to send the recovery message — all of which are CRM/telephony operations. The fetch.py reads exclusively from the TrustPager phone call-logs endpoint (api_get on the resolved "phone" call-logs path), does contact/opportunity enrichment against CRM contacts and deals, and the send step routes through send_sms/send_email. There is no realistic offline source for "which calls did I miss in the last 24h, and did I already call them back": a phone number alone (from a screenshot or paste) gives you a number to text, but loses the recovery's core mechanics — the time-since-missed urgency ranking, the dedup-by-number, the already-recovered detection, the caller-identity-and-open-deal context that decides the message, and the actual send channel. The reasoning/drafting rules (quiet-hours fallback to email, no fabricated names, don't open with "sorry I missed your call" after 6h) are reusable copy logic, but they are a thin wrapper with nothing to operate on once the live call feed is removed. Speed-to-lead on missed calls IS a phone/CRM operation; it does not stand up on local files, owner paste, or pure reasoning.
missed-call-recovery.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not merely an enhancer here — it is the substrate the skill runs on. Connected, it supplies the missed-inbound-call feed (phone call logs with direction/status/disposition/duration), identifies each caller against the contact database, surfaces the linked open opportunity and its pipeline stage to shape the message, computes already-recovered status by scanning for a later outbound or answered-inbound call to the same number, and provides the send_sms/send_email rails to actually deliver the recovery message under per-message approval. If TrustPager (or an equivalent connected phone/CRM system exposing call logs, contacts, and a send channel) is absent, the skill has no data to act on and no way to act — so it lives behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section rather than in the general floor or extractable set.

nurture-health.current_function: Health-checks the operator's LIVE nurture/drip auto queues: for each queue it reports the enrolment funnel (enrolled → active → completed → cancelled), which step is leaking the most people, per-step open/click rates from email logs, and whether the un-enrol side is firing. Read-only diagnose; hands fixes to design/wire/lint/why-didnt-it-fire.
nurture-health.standalone_value: Minimal standalone value. The entire output is a live read of CRM automation state — enrolment records and their per-enrolment progress (last completed step), status mix (active/completed/cancelled/removed), per-step "reached" counts, auto-queue step definitions, and email-log engagement keyed by automation_id. None of this exists for an owner with nothing connected: a funnel is a property of a running enrolment engine, not a file an owner has lying around. fetch.py is built entirely on TrustPager endpoints (list_auto_queues/get_auto_queue/get_auto_queue_board/list_auto_queue_enrollments/list_email_logs) with no non-CRM data path. The reasoning layer (how to read a leak, what fix to offer) is reusable, but it has nothing to operate on without the live queue + enrolment + engagement data, so the skill collapses without a CRM. This is the same CRM-operation family as wire-nurture-sequence and why-didnt-it-fire — the diagnostic counterpart to them. (Pure drafting like design-nurture-sequence would be the general_floor sibling; this is not that.)
nurture-health.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The skill IS the act of sweeping the live auto-queue/event-queue system: resolving the queue endpoint, paginating enrolments to build the funnel and per-step reached counts, detecting whether the un-enrol/cancel side is firing, flagging stalled-active enrolments, and joining email logs to step automations for open/click rates. Remove the CRM and there is no funnel, no enrolment statuses, and no automation-linked engagement to report. It belongs squarely behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section as the diagnostic that closes the loop design + wire leave open.

onboard-team-member.current_function: Generates a per-hire onboarding pack (their own CLAUDE.md + a memory pack + a role-scoped command list) into ./team/<name>/ by reading the single team-standards.md file, the owner's ./CLAUDE.md, and the knowledge/ voice + safeguards files — so every team member runs Claude Code on the same voice, the same verify-before-it-ships gate, and clear role boundaries without anyone re-explaining it each session.
onboard-team-member.standalone_value: This is pure local-file generation plus reasoning — there is NO fetch.py and NOT a single TrustPager MCP call anywhere in the workflow. It reads templates/team-standards.md, the owner's ./CLAUDE.md, and knowledge/communication-voice.md + knowledge/safeguards.md, then writes the new person's CLAUDE.md, memory files (team-voice, verify-first, role-and-approvals), and a role-scoped commands.md. A solo owner or small team with nothing connected gets the full minute-one win: codify your team's standards once, and every new hire's Claude setup carries the same customer voice, the same verify-first discipline, and explicit can/cannot role boundaries from day one — replacing the evaporating "paste it into their chat each time" pattern with persistent per-machine standards. None of the core value depends on a live CRM; the three TrustPager mentions are incidental (the "email" doubles as a TrustPager login, and the handoff install steps tell the hire to connect their own TrustPager key) — strip them and the skill still fully delivers.
onboard-team-member.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager IS connected, onboarding extends from "set up their Claude config" to "set up their actual seat": the owner's email becomes a real TrustPager login, and the handoff step where the new hire connects their own workspace key means the role-scoped command list (e.g. an sdr getting draft-only /draft-reply but no /automate-this) maps onto live, enforced workspace permissions and pipeline access — the can/cannot boundaries become real CRM guardrails, not just guidance. A future enhancement could also read live workspace users/roles to auto-detect role rows or pre-provision the seat via invite_user. But all of that DEEPENS a skill that already stands fully on its own from local files.

outstanding-documents.current_function: Per-client document reconciliation: reads the file-upload fields on forms sent to each client plus files on the deal record, builds a received/missing checklist per client, ranks the chase by how overdue the missing docs are, and offers to draft a reminder or resend the form (with approval). Document-level companion to /form-radar's form-level view.
outstanding-documents.standalone_value: The core value is reconciliation + triage: take "what each client was asked for" vs "what's actually arrived," produce a chase-first checklist that names the EXACT missing document (not "your form's incomplete"), rank clients by how overdue they are, and surface the single most valuable chase to make first — plus draft the reminder wording. None of that reasoning requires a CRM. A broker/accountant/lawyer who keeps a simple tracker (client | docs requested | docs received | date asked) or a per-client folder of received files can get the full checklist, the overdue ranking, and ready-to-send reminder text from this skill alone. It honours the same hard rules standalone (don't guess a doc is required when no checklist exists; don't chase clients who've supplied everything; name exact docs). It is genuinely useful with nothing connected — it's a reconciliation/triage task, not a live-CRM mutation, so it ships as a general-purpose skill.
outstanding-documents.tp_enhancement: TrustPager turns a manual, owner-maintained checklist into an automatic, always-current one. Connected, it derives "requested" from the actual file-upload fields on forms sent to each client (list_form_submissions(?deal_id=) + get_form_submission) and any on-record checklist, and "received" from list_opportunity_files(deal_id) (portal uploads land here automatically) plus file fields that now hold a file — so the owner never has to hand-build the tracker. It scopes to the right pipeline stages, computes the "asked Nd ago" overdue clock from live timestamps, and makes the chase one-click: resend_form_submission to re-fire the original request, or hand to /automate-this to auto-remind after N days. Standalone gives the analysis; TrustPager gives live data plus the ability to actually act on it inside the workspace.

outstanding-invoices.current_function: Confirms a connected accounting integration (Xero) and queries TrustPager's Invoices/Receivables report source for the open-AR ledger (status=AUTHORISED, amount_due>0), then presents an aged-bucket summary (Current/1-30/31-60/61-90/90+) plus the most-overdue invoices. Branches on integration state: not-connected (stop and prompt to connect), connected-but-unseeded (offer one-time sync_receivables catch-up), or connected-with-data (present the picture). Optionally wires a daily emailed AR digest via create_report_dashboard + add_report_card + send_report_email + an auto_schedule cron.
outstanding-invoices.standalone_value: The core deliverable — an aged accounts-receivable summary plus a "chase these first" list — is pure reasoning over a set of invoice rows (invoice #, customer, due date, amount due, paid/unpaid). That bucketing-by-days-overdue, total-exposure, worst-offender ranking needs no CRM; it computes identically from a Xero/QuickBooks CSV export or a simple invoices spreadsheet. Cash flow is the operator's #1 worry, so it lands a real minute-one win standalone.
outstanding-invoices.tp_enhancement: TrustPager turns a one-off pasted export into a live auto-refreshing receivables ledger (always current after a one-time seed), and unlocks Step 3 — a persistent dashboard plus send_report_email on an auto_schedule cron that emails the aged AR digest to owner and bookkeeper every morning server-side. It also enables sending approved chase emails/SMS to overdue debtors directly.

prep-for-call.current_function: Builds a pre-call brief for the operator: identifies the call, pulls the full picture (opportunity stage/value, recent activity history, last call transcript, open tasks, contact details, quoted products) and synthesizes it into one scannable read — who they are, where the deal's at, what was said last time, what's open/owed, risks to watch, and the single outcome to drive. Read-only; offers follow-ons (draft agenda, pull proposal) but doesn't write anything. Sources all inputs from TrustPager MCP tools (list_bookings, get_booking, search_contacts/opportunities, get_opportunity, get_opportunity_activities, list_transcripts, get_opportunity_tasks, get_contact, get_opportunity_products).
prep-for-call.standalone_value: The genuine value is the synthesis, not the data fetch: turning scattered facts about a person and a deal into one 5-minute-read brief that ends in a single outcome to drive — instead of a menu of options. That reasoning (assemble who / where-it's-at / last-time / open-and-owed / watch-for / the one outcome) is pure judgement and works on whatever the owner can supply. A solo owner with no CRM can paste their last email thread, dictate "I'm seeing the Hendersons at 2, we quoted them the deck job 3 weeks ago and they went quiet," or point at a local notes file / calendar export, and still walk away with a structured, walk-in-ready brief. The skill is also explicitly read-only, so nothing about it is a live CRM operation — it's a research-and-summarize pattern that just happens to read from TrustPager today. Strip TrustPager and the brief still lands; it just leans on owner-supplied history instead of an auto-pulled record.
prep-for-call.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected the skill goes from "as good as what the owner remembers to paste" to "complete and effortless." It auto-resolves the call from today's bookings, follows the opportunity as the hub, and pulls the full objective record in parallel: stage/value/owner, the recent activity timeline, open tasks (what's owed), the contact's relationship age, and what's been quoted. Critically it surfaces the last call transcript — the single highest-value input — so LAST TIME reflects what was actually said and promised rather than a generic guess. It also powers the WATCH-FOR line with real signals (gone quiet N days, overdue item, declined quote) the owner might not recall. So TrustPager removes the prep work and raises fidelity; it deepens the brief but is not required to produce one.

quote-from-photo.current_function: Turns an operator-supplied site photo (plus a voice memo transcript or typed notes) into a drafted quote: reads scope off the image, lists assumptions and unknowns, builds a scope + line-item table, and writes a proposal in the operator's voice for review. Drafts only — it does not commit anything. Optionally calls TrustPager list_products to match catalogue names/prices, and points at downstream skills (build-document, send-for-signing, attach to opportunity) for the hand-off.
quote-from-photo.standalone_value: Delivers its core minute-one win with zero tools connected: the value is vision + reasoning over inputs the owner supplies directly. The operator attaches the photo and dictates/types a few notes; the model reads the image, describes quote-relevant scope, separates what it sees from what it assumes, builds line items, and drafts the proposal text. None of that requires a CRM. The SKILL.md already specifies the no-TrustPager path explicitly: "If you don't have their price list, draft the scope + line-item structure and leave the prices for the operator to drop in — flag that clearly rather than guessing rates." It is draft-only by design (a hard rule), so nothing about its primary output depends on writing to or reading from a live workspace.
quote-from-photo.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected, list_products lets the draft pull the operator's real catalogue — exact product names and current rates — so line items and pricing match their book instead of being left blank for manual fill-in. TrustPager also unlocks the optional downstream hand-off the skill points to but never does on its own: creating/finding the opportunity and attaching products via add_opportunity_product, saving the proposal as a note/document, or converting it into a signing envelope (build-document → send-for-signing). So TrustPager turns a self-contained draft into a priced, attachable, sendable deal artifact — a deepening, not a requirement.

report-an-issue.current_function: Captures a bug report or feature request from the operator, classifies it (bug vs feature vs how-to question), gathers just enough detail to make it actionable, and files it as a structured service request to the TrustPager team via create_service_request, then confirms what happens next.
report-an-issue.standalone_value: Minimal standalone value. The reasoning layer (deciding bug vs feature, prompting for expected-vs-actual/repro/priority or use-case/outcome) is mildly reusable as a report-structuring helper, but the skill's actual deliverable — a filed, tracked report that a vendor team receives, investigates, fixes, verifies, and reports back on — does not exist without the CRM. With nothing connected there is no recipient and no queue: the report has nowhere to go and no one acts on it, so the promised outcome ("the team fixes it and tells you how to use it") collapses. Writing the report to a local file would be a hollow imitation that delivers no real benefit.
report-an-issue.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the entire mechanism. The value IS the CRM operation: create_service_request files into the TrustPager team's live service-request queue with category (bug_report/feature_request) and priority, links the relevant record id, returns HTTP 202 when queued for approval, and feeds the team's investigate-fix-verify-notify loop. Remove TrustPager and the skill has no destination, no tracking, and no resolution path. It belongs squarely behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section.

review-team-draft.current_function: A manager-side review gate: lists teammates' customer-facing drafts awaiting approval (from the local ./team/_drafts/ registry, or pasted in), shows each draft plus its linked record, scores it against two bars — (1) is the claim verified working, (2) is it in team voice per knowledge/communication-voice.md — then either approves (marking it ready or sending via email/SMS) or returns it with a specific coaching note, moving the entry to _approved/ or _returned/. The human half of the verify-before-customer gate.
review-team-draft.standalone_value: The skill's core is human review judgment, not a CRM operation. Strip TrustPager and everything load-bearing survives: drafts live in the local ./team/_drafts/ registry (and the SKILL.md explicitly allows a draft to be "pasted straight in for review"); the two quality bars are scored against local files (knowledge/communication-voice.md, knowledge/safeguards.md, templates/team-standards.md), all confirmed present in the repo with no TrustPager dependency; approve/return + the coaching note + moving the entry to _approved/_returned/ are pure local file operations. The value — catching off-voice or unverified messages before they reach customers and teaching the author the standard — lands fully without anything connected. TrustPager is only touched in two peripheral spots, both with documented non-TP fallbacks.
review-team-draft.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected it deepens the review in two ways. (1) Context: Step 2 pulls the linked opportunity/contact via get_opportunity/get_contact so the reviewer can judge whether the message fits the live situation, instead of relying on what the author pasted.
