(2) Delivery: on approve, if the channel is email/SMS, the message sends straight through the platform (send_email/send_sms) and respects its approval gates (a 202 surfaces the platform approval link). Without TrustPager the reviewer judges fit from the pasted/local context and the approved draft is marked ready for the author to send — same review value, manual send.

send-email.current_function: Wraps the TrustPager send_email/reply_to_email tools: pulls full context via fetch.py (contact record, recent email threads with the contact, the workspace's last few sent emails for tone calibration, and the active email config/signature), drafts the body in the workspace tone, reply-vs-new-thread logic, attachment resolution from opportunity files, quiet-hours scheduling, approve-before-send, then sends and logs on the opportunity.
send-email.standalone_value: The core value is "draft and send a well-formed, on-tone email with a human approval gate" — a universal small-business task, not inherently a CRM operation. Standalone, the skill still delivers the high-value part: the drafting discipline (first-name address, reference one concrete thing from context, one main message, one clear ask, tone matching from sample emails, no vague pronouns) plus the safety rails (show To/CC/subject/body and wait for explicit yes, one email per invocation, quiet-hours awareness, ask before CCing others). With nothing connected, the owner pastes the prior thread or describes the situation and the recipient; Claude reads any local sample emails for tone and returns a polished, ready-to-paste draft (or sends/schedules it through a connected generic email tool). The send mechanism is just a transport that can be swapped.
send-email.tp_enhancement: When TrustPager is connected it deepens every step: fetch.py auto-pulls the contact record so no manual lookup is needed; it detects an existing thread and routes to reply_to_email (correct subject + threading) instead of starting a new one; it samples the workspace's recent sent emails for accurate tone calibration; it injects the configured sender + signature automatically; it resolves attachments from opportunity files; it sends through the workspace email config and logs the email as activity on the opportunity; and quiet-hours sends route through schedule_communication. So TrustPager turns a paste-and-draft helper into a fully-wired, logged, threaded send — but the drafting and approval value lands without it.

send-for-signing.current_function: Sends a TrustPager document template to one or more signers on an opportunity, creating a tracked e-signature envelope that emails recipients a hosted signing page, threads tracking onto the deal, and emits live signature_opened / signature_completed signals (hand-off to /signing-radar and /automate-this).
send-for-signing.standalone_value: Minimal-to-none standalone. The value IS an e-signature + CRM operation, not document drafting. Every load-bearing step is a live platform action: it requires a template_id from TrustPager document templates, a deal_id from a TrustPager opportunity, calls send_for_signing to mint a tracked envelope, hosts the signing page TrustPager emails to the recipient, threads the envelope onto the opportunity, and relies on TrustPager's signature_opened/signature_completed event signals for the tracking and follow-on automation. Strip TrustPager away and there is no swappable data source that rescues it — Claude Code reasoning over local files cannot send a legally binding signature request, host a signer page, or track open/sign status. A standalone owner would need a different e-signature service entirely (DocuSign/Dropbox Sign), which is replacing the engine, not changing the data source. Document drafting itself lives in the separate /build-document skill, which this one redirects to; this skill is purely the send-and-track action. Belongs behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section.
send-for-signing.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the entire mechanism. It supplies the document template, the opportunity the envelope attaches to, the e-signature envelope creation and hosted signer page, the email delivery to recipients, the per-recipient sent/opened/completed tracking, the approval gate (202) safeguard, and the downstream signals that power /signing-radar and the signature_opened automation. Without it the skill has no action to perform.

show-me-how.current_function: Turns a plain-English "how do I X?" into a hands-on walkthrough OF TRUSTPAGER: pre-fetches the workspace's AI instructions and custom training canvases (Learning Hub) via fetch.py, searches the TrustPager help center (search_help_center), falls back to describe_resource/describe_action_type to reason from the schema, then distills the answer into numbered steps + the exact app.trustpager.com workspace URL + one gotcha, and offers to drive the task via the relevant mcp__trustpager__* tool (or file a feature request via create_service_request).
show-me-how.standalone_value: Effectively none. Every layer of this skill is bound to TrustPager: the subject matter is "how to use TrustPager," the search corpus is the TrustPager help center, the schema fallback is TrustPager's describe_resource/describe_action_type, the pre-fetch (fetch.py) pulls TrustPager AI instructions + TrustPager training canvases, every deliverable is an app.trustpager.com URL, and the "want me to do it for you?" offer executes mcp__trustpager__* tools. Strip TrustPager and there is no product to explain, no help center to search, no schema to introspect, no workspace page to link, and nothing to drive. It is a guided-tour-and-operate-your-CRM skill, not a generic "teach me a business task" skill — so it does not deliver meaningful standalone value to an owner with nothing connected.
show-me-how.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the entire substrate. The skill's value (surfacing the right help-center article + workspace overlay, linking the exact workspace page, and optionally executing the operation live) only exists when TrustPager is connected. It belongs squarely behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section as a native CRM how-to/guided-action skill.

signing-radar.current_function: Tracks the e-signature funnel across every document sent for signing — sent → opened → signed — and buckets the follow-ups by urgency: opened-but-not-signed (engaged, hottest), sent-but-never-opened-going-stale (chase), declined, and recently completed. Then offers next steps: resend/nudge an unopened envelope, draft a follow-up to an opened-not-signed signer, or void a dead one (with approval). Data source is entirely TrustPager's list_signing_envelopes (read-only), reading per-envelope status + sent/created timestamps.
signing-radar.standalone_value: The value IS a CRM/e-signature operation and collapses without the connector. The skill's whole engine is per-envelope open/sign telemetry — "opened twice but never signed", "sent 9 days ago, never opened" — which only exists inside the platform that sent the documents and tracks signer events (view pings, sign events, decline reasons). There is no realistic standalone source for this funnel: an owner with nothing connected knows what they emailed and whether a signed PDF came back, but cannot reconstruct who-opened-but-didn't-sign or the sent→opened→signed funnel from local files, a pasted export, or memory — the open/decline signals simply aren't captured anywhere they control. The follow-up actions (resend_signing_envelope, void_signing_envelope) are also live envelope mutations. A generic "list documents I'm waiting on, oldest first" reminder could be built standalone, but that is a different, far weaker skill (no open/sign distinction, which is the entire point here — the "opened but not signed" gold bucket is what drives the InsureHQ call-them-while-hot play). Honestly classifying this as extractable would pollute the floor: stripping TrustPager removes the funnel, the hottest-follow-up signal, and the actions, leaving almost nothing.
signing-radar.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not an enhancement here — it is the substrate. The connector supplies the entire dataset (every envelope with live status and timestamps via list_signing_envelopes), the open/sign event tracking that distinguishes "opened-not-signed" from "never-opened", and the write actions the skill offers (resend_signing_envelope to nudge a stale one, void_signing_envelope to kill a dead one). It also links each envelope to its deal_id, enabling the handoff to /draft-reply and to /automate-this on the signature_opened trigger for "follow up automatically every time someone opens a document". This skill belongs behind the optional connect-TrustPager section.

sync-team-standards.current_function: After the owner edits templates/team-standards.md (voice, verify rule, roles, approval thresholds), this re-generates every existing team member's pack (their CLAUDE.md + memory/*.md + commands.md) from the updated standards, shows a per-person diff, and writes only on confirmation — closing the loop so a standards change reaches the whole team, not just new hires. It also flags people in the standards with no pack and packs with no matching person, and produces a re-pull note for affected members.
sync-team-standards.standalone_value: Delivers full value with zero tools connected. It is pure local-file + reasoning work: it reads local files (templates/team-standards.md, knowledge/communication-voice.md, knowledge/safeguards.md, the owner's ./CLAUDE.md), enumerates local ./team/<slug>/ pack folders, regenerates each pack in memory, diffs against what is on disk, and writes the updated CLAUDE.md/memory files back locally on confirmation. There is no fetch.py and the SKILL.md makes no TrustPager/MCP calls. Standards flow one way from a local markdown file into local packs — the keep-the-whole-team-in-sync benefit lands entirely on the local filesystem. It is the natural companion to /onboard-team-member and shares its file-only model.
sync-team-standards.tp_enhancement: TrustPager is not a data source for this skill, but when connected it can validate and enrich the sync: cross-check each pack's role/approval thresholds in team-standards against the member's actual workspace role and permission scope (get_workspace_user_roles / list_company_users) so a regenerated pack never grants more than the CRM allows; confirm that each section-5 person is a real workspace user (flagging stale packs for people who have left); and optionally push the change-summary/re-pull note to the affected teammate via send_email or send_sms instead of the owner forwarding it manually. The core regenerate-diff-and-write loop still works fully without any of this.

test-form.current_function: Pre-flight safety check for a TrustPager form or client portal: verifies the form's CRM field mapping, sends a test to the operator or a dedicated test contact (never a real client), walks them through submitting it, confirms each answer wrote back onto the right CRM field, then offers to clean up the test record.
test-form.tp_enhancement: This skill IS the TrustPager-native capability, so TrustPager is the enabling layer rather than an enhancement. When connected it supplies: the form/portal template and its CRM field wiring to flag unmapped fields up front; send_form / portal-share to deliver a safe test; the approval queue (202 = queued) to respect; and read-back of the test contact/opportunity to confirm field-by-field write-back, plus delete tools to clean up the test data afterwards. It lives behind the optional "connect TrustPager" section — without it, there is nothing to test.
